412: // HasBody returns true if the request declares a body via Content-Length, Transfer-Encoding, or already buffered payload data.
413: func (c *DefaultCtx) HasBody() bool {
414: 	hdr := &c.fasthttp.Request.Header
415: 
416: 	switch cl := hdr.ContentLength(); {
417: 	case cl > 0:
418: 		return true
419: 	case cl == -1:
420: 		// fasthttp reports -1 for Transfer-Encoding: chunked bodies.
421: 		return true
422: 	case cl == 0:
423: 		if hasTransferEncodingBody(hdr) {
424: 			return true
425: 		}

428: 	return len(c.fasthttp.Request.Body()) > 0

432: // If the parameter name does not exist in the route, this method does nothing.
433: func (c *DefaultCtx) OverrideParam(name, value string) {
434: 	// If no route is matched, there are no parameters to update
435: 	if !c.Matched() {
436: 		return
437: 	}
438: 
439: 	// Normalize wildcard (*) and plus (+) tokens to their internal
440: 	// representations (*1, +1) used by the router.
441: 	if name == "*" || name == "+" {
442: 		name += "1"
443: 	}
444: 
445: 	if c.app.config.CaseSensitive {
446: 		for i, param := range c.route.Params {
447: 			if param == name {
448: 				c.values[i] = value
449: 				return
450: 			}
451: 		}
452: 		return
453: 	}
454: 
455: 	nameBytes := utils.UnsafeBytes(name)
456: 	for i, param := range c.route.Params {
457: 		if utils.EqualFold(utils.UnsafeBytes(param), nameBytes) {
458: 			c.values[i] = value
459: 			return
460: 		}
461: 	}

464: func hasTransferEncodingBody(hdr *fasthttp.RequestHeader) bool {
465: 	// Repeated field lines form one combined list (RFC 9110 Section 5.2),
466: 	// so every Transfer-Encoding line must be inspected, not just the first.
467: 	if lines := hdr.PeekAll(HeaderTransferEncoding); len(lines) > 0 {
468: 		for _, line := range lines {
469: 			if transferEncodingLineHasBody(utils.UnsafeString(line)) {
470: 				return true
471: 			}
472: 		}
473: 		return false
474: 	}
475: 
476: 	// Fallback scan for non-normalized header keys.
477: 	for key, value := range hdr.All() {
478: 		if !utils.EqualFold(utils.UnsafeString(key), HeaderTransferEncoding) {
479: 			continue
480: 		}
481: 		if transferEncodingLineHasBody(utils.UnsafeString(value)) {
482: 			return true
483: 		}
484: 	}
485: 
486: 	return false
487: }

489: // transferEncodingLineHasBody reports whether a single Transfer-Encoding
490: // field line contains a transfer coding other than "identity".
491: func transferEncodingLineHasBody(te string) bool {
492: 	for raw := range strings.SplitSeq(te, ",") {
493: 		token := utils.TrimSpace(raw)
494: 		if token == "" {
495: 			continue
496: 		}
497: 		if idx := strings.IndexByte(token, ';'); idx >= 0 {
498: 			token = utils.TrimSpace(token[:idx])
499: 		}
500: 		if token == "" {
501: 			continue
502: 		}
503: 		if utils.EqualFold(token, "identity") {
504: 			continue
505: 		}
506: 		return true
507: 	}
508: 	return false
509: }

511: // IsWebSocket returns true if the request includes a WebSocket upgrade handshake.
512: func (c *DefaultCtx) IsWebSocket() bool {
513: 	// Repeated field lines are equivalent to one combined comma-separated
514: 	// list (RFC 9110 Section 5.2), so inspect every Connection and Upgrade
515: 	// field line, not just the first.
516: 	if !headerListContainsToken(c.fasthttp.Request.Header.PeekAll(HeaderConnection), "upgrade") {
517: 		return false
518: 	}
519: 	// Upgrade is a list of protocols, each optionally carrying a "/version"
520: 	// suffix (RFC 9110 Section 7.8), e.g. "Upgrade: websocket, h2c".
521: 	return headerListContainsToken(c.fasthttp.Request.Header.PeekAll(HeaderUpgrade), "websocket")
522: }

524: // headerListContainsToken reports whether any comma-separated element across
525: // the given field lines equals token case-insensitively. An optional
526: // "/version" suffix (Upgrade protocol syntax, RFC 9110 Section 7.8) is
527: // ignored when comparing; valid Connection members never contain "/", so
528: // this is safe for both headers.

144: // Body contains the raw body submitted in a POST request.
145: // This method will decompress the body if the 'Content-Encoding' header is provided.
146: // It returns the original (or decompressed) body data which is valid only within the handler.
147: // Don't store direct references to the returned data.
148: // If you need to keep the body's data later, make a copy or use the Immutable option.
149: func (r *DefaultReq) Body() []byte {
150: 	var (
151: 		err                error
152: 		body, originalBody []byte
153: 		headerEncoding     string
154: 		encodingOrder      = []string{"", "", ""}
155: 	)
156: 
157: 	request := &r.c.fasthttp.Request
158: 
159: 	// Fast path: no Content-Encoding header at all. ContentEncoding uses the
160: 	// pre-normalized key constant, so absence costs a single cheap lookup.
161: 	// An empty value is still a present field line and must be joined with
162: 	// duplicates below before RFC 9110 empty-list elements are ignored.
163: 	if request.Header.ContentEncoding() == nil {
164: 		return r.getBody()
165: 	}
166: 
167: 	// Get Content-Encoding header. Multiple field lines form one combined
168: 	// list (RFC 9110 Section 5.2), so join them before splitting.
169: 	encodedBytes, _ := peekJoinedRequestHeader(&request.Header, HeaderContentEncoding)
170: 	headerEncoding = utils.UnsafeString(utilsbytes.UnsafeToLower(encodedBytes))
171: 
172: 	// Split and get the encodings list, in order to attend the
173: 	// rule defined at: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110#section-8.4-5
174: 	// The splitter drops empty list elements (RFC 9110 Section 5.6.1.2), and
175: 	// headerEncoding was already lowercased wholesale above.
176: 	encodingOrder = getSplicedStrList(headerEncoding, encodingOrder)
177: 	if len(encodingOrder) == 0 {
178: 		return r.getBody()
179: 	}
180: 
181: 	var decodesRealized uint8
182: 	body, decodesRealized, err = r.tryDecodeBodyInOrder(&originalBody, encodingOrder)
183: 
184: 	// Ensure that the body will be the original
185: 	if originalBody != nil && decodesRealized > 0 {
186: 		request.SetBodyRaw(originalBody)
187: 	}
188: 	if err != nil {
189: 		switch {
190: 		case errors.Is(err, ErrUnsupportedMediaType):
191: 			_ = r.c.DefaultRes.SendStatus(StatusUnsupportedMediaType) //nolint:errcheck,staticcheck // It is fine to ignore the error and the static check
192: 		case errors.Is(err, ErrNotImplemented):
193: 			_ = r.c.DefaultRes.SendStatus(StatusNotImplemented) //nolint:errcheck,staticcheck // It is fine to ignore the error and the static check
194: 		case errors.Is(err, fasthttp.ErrBodyTooLarge):
195: 			_ = r.c.DefaultRes.SendStatus(StatusRequestEntityTooLarge) //nolint:errcheck,staticcheck // It is fine to ignore the error and the static check
196: 		default:
197: 			// do nothing
198: 		}
199: 		return []byte(err.Error())
200: 	}
201: 
202: 	return r.c.app.GetBytes(body)
203: }

266: // Charset returns the charset parameter from the Content-Type header.
267: func (c *DefaultCtx) Charset() string {
268: 	contentType := c.fasthttp.Request.Header.ContentType()
269: 	_, params, ok := bytes.Cut(contentType, []byte{';'})
270: 	if !ok {
271: 		return ""
272: 	}
273: 	for len(params) > 0 {
274: 		// Slice off the next parameter at the next ";" that sits outside a
275: 		// quoted-string: parameter values may be quoted and contain ";"
276: 		// (RFC 9110 Section 5.6.6). A DQUOTE only opens a quoted-string at
277: 		// the start of a value (after an "=" plus optional whitespace), so a
278: 		// stray quote later in an unquoted value cannot swallow the rest of
279: 		// the header.
280: 		param := params
281: 		end := -1
282: 		inQuotes := false
283: 		escaped := false
284: 		expectValue := false
285: 	scan:
286: 		for i := 0; i < len(params); i++ {
287: 			ch := params[i]
288: 			switch {
289: 			case escaped:
290: 				escaped = false
291: 			case inQuotes:
292: 				switch ch {
293: 				case '\\':
294: 					escaped = true
295: 				case '"':
296: 					inQuotes = false
297: 				}
298: 			case ch == '=':
299: 				expectValue = true
300: 			case ch == '"' && expectValue:
301: 				inQuotes = true
302: 				expectValue = false
303: 			case ch == ';':
304: 				end = i
305: 				break scan
306: 			case ch != ' ' && ch != '\t':
307: 				expectValue = false
308: 			}
309: 		}
310: 		if end >= 0 {
311: 			param = params[:end]
312: 			params = params[end+1:]
313: 		} else {
314: 			params = nil
315: 		}
316: 
317: 		name, value, ok := bytes.Cut(param, []byte{'='})
318: 		if !ok || !utils.EqualFold(utils.TrimSpace(name), []byte("charset")) {
319: 			continue
320: 		}
321: 		v := utils.TrimSpace(value)
322: 		if len(v) > 0 && v[0] == '"' {
323: 			// A quoted value must be a complete quoted-string, and its
324: 			// quoted-pairs must be replaced with the escaped octet
325: 			// (RFC 9110 Section 5.6.4).
326: 			if len(v) < 2 || v[len(v)-1] != '"' {
327: 				return ""
328: 			}
329: 			unescaped, err := unescapeHeaderValue(v[1 : len(v)-1])
330: 			if err != nil {
331: 				return ""
332: 			}
333: 			v = unescaped
334: 		} else if bytes.IndexByte(v, '"') >= 0 {
335: 			// A bare token must not contain DQUOTE; skip the invalid
336: 			// parameter instead of surfacing garbage, so a well-formed
337: 			// charset parameter later in the header can still be found.
338: 			continue
339: 		}
340: 		return c.app.toString(v)
341: 	}
342: 	return ""
343: }

439: // Fresh returns true when the response is still “fresh” in the client's cache,
440: // otherwise false is returned to indicate that the client cache is now stale
441: // and the full response should be sent.
442: // Freshness only applies to GET and HEAD requests; for any other method false is
443: // returned, as RFC 9110 defines 304 Not Modified only for those methods and
444: // requires If-Modified-Since to be ignored otherwise.
445: // When a client sends the Cache-Control: no-cache request header to indicate an end-to-end
446: // reload request, this module will return false to make handling these requests transparent.
447: // https://github.com/jshttp/fresh/blob/master/index.js#L33
448: func (r *DefaultReq) Fresh() bool {
449: 	// Freshness only applies to GET and HEAD requests: a 304 Not Modified
450: 	// response is defined for those methods only, and RFC 9110 Section 13.1.3
451: 	// requires If-Modified-Since to be ignored for any other method.
452: 	// A negative methodInt means the method is not registered at all, so it
453: 	// cannot be GET or HEAD (and must not be used to index RequestMethods).
454: 	if r.c.methodInt < 0 {
455: 		return false
456: 	}
457: 	if method := r.c.app.method(r.c.methodInt); method != MethodGet && method != MethodHead {
458: 		return false
459: 	}
460: 
461: 	header := &r.c.fasthttp.Request.Header
462: 
463: 	// fields
464: 	// List-based fields may be split across multiple field lines, which are
465: 	// semantically one comma-joined list (RFC 9110 Section 5.2).
466: 	modifiedSince := header.Peek(HeaderIfModifiedSince)
467: 	noneMatch := joinHeaderValues(header.PeekAll(HeaderIfNoneMatch))
468: 
469: 	// unconditional request
470: 	if len(modifiedSince) == 0 && len(noneMatch) == 0 {
471: 		return false
472: 	}
473: 
474: 	// Always return stale when Cache-Control: no-cache
475: 	// to support end-to-end reload requests
476: 	// https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9111#section-5.2.1.4
477: 	cacheControl := joinHeaderValues(header.PeekAll(HeaderCacheControl))
478: 	if len(cacheControl) > 0 && isNoCache(utils.UnsafeString(cacheControl)) {
479: 		return false
480: 	}
481: 
482: 	// if-none-match takes precedence over if-modified-since (RFC 9110)
483: 	if len(noneMatch) > 0 {
484: 		if len(noneMatch) == 1 && noneMatch[0] == '*' {
485: 			return true
486: 		}
487: 		app := r.c.app
488: 		response := &r.c.fasthttp.Response
489: 		etag := app.toString(response.Header.Peek(HeaderETag))
490: 		if etag == "" {
491: 			return false
492: 		}
493: 		if app.isEtagStale(etag, noneMatch) {
494: 			return false
495: 		}
496: 		return true
497: 	}
498: 
499: 	// if-modified-since (only reached when if-none-match is absent)
500: 	if len(modifiedSince) > 0 {
501: 		response := &r.c.fasthttp.Response
502: 		lastModified := response.Header.Peek(HeaderLastModified)
503: 		if len(lastModified) == 0 {
504: 			return false
505: 		}
506: 		lastModifiedTime, err := parseHTTPDate(lastModified)
507: 		if err != nil {
508: 			return false
509: 		}
510: 		// Common conditional request: the client echoes back the exact
511: 		// Last-Modified it was given. Identical, already-validated dates are
512: 		// equal, so skip the second parse and comparison.
513: 		if !bytes.Equal(lastModified, modifiedSince) {
514: 			modifiedSinceTime, err := parseHTTPDate(modifiedSince)
515: 			if err != nil {
516: 				return false
517: 			}
518: 			if lastModifiedTime.Compare(modifiedSinceTime) == 1 {
519: 				return false
520: 			}
521: 		}
522: 	}
523: 	return true
524: }

707: // extractIPFromHeader returns the client IP from the given proxy header by walking the
708: // X-Forwarded-For chain from right to left and stripping trusted proxy IPs. When trusted
709: // proxies are configured, the rightmost non-trusted IP is returned; otherwise the first
710: // valid IP (left-to-right) is returned. When IP validation is disabled, the raw header
711: // value is returned as-is.
712: func (r *DefaultReq) extractIPFromHeader(header string) string {
713: 	app := r.c.app
714: 
715: 	if !app.config.EnableIPValidation {
716: 		return r.Get(header)
717: 	}
718: 
719: 	headerValue := r.Get(header)
720: 	hasTrustedProxyConfig := r.hasTrustedProxyConfig()
721: 	if !hasTrustedProxyConfig {
722: 		start := 0
723: 		for {
724: 			end := start
725: 			for end < len(headerValue) && headerValue[end] != ',' {
726: 				end++
727: 			}
728: 
729: 			ipStr := utils.Trim(headerValue[start:end], ' ')
730: 			if isValidProxyIP(ipStr) {
731: 				return ipStr
732: 			}
733: 			if end == len(headerValue) {
734: 				break
735: 			}
736: 			start = end + 1
737: 		}
738: 	}
739: 
740: 	var leftmostIP string
741: 
742: 	for end := len(headerValue); end > 0; {
743: 		start := end
744: 		for start > 0 && headerValue[start-1] != ',' {
745: 			start--
746: 		}
747: 
748: 		ipStr := utils.Trim(headerValue[start:end], ' ')
749: 		if isValidProxyIP(ipStr) {
750: 			leftmostIP = ipStr
751: 			if !r.isTrustedProxyIP(ipStr) {
752: 				return ipStr
753: 			}
754: 		}
755: 
756: 		if start == 0 {
757: 			break
758: 		}
759: 		end = start - 1
760: 	}
761: 
762: 	if leftmostIP != "" {
763: 		return leftmostIP
764: 	}
765: 	if ip := r.c.fasthttp.RemoteIP(); ip != nil {
766: 		return ip.String()
767: 	}
768: 	return ""
769: }

785: // isTrustedProxyIP checks whether the given IP string matches any configured trusted proxy.
786: func (r *DefaultReq) isTrustedProxyIP(ipStr string) bool {
787: 	cfg := r.c.app.config.TrustProxyConfig
788: 
789: 	// utils.ParseIPv4/ParseIPv6 together accept exactly the strings
790: 	// netip.ParseAddr does, without allocating an error for invalid input.
791: 	ip, ok := utils.ParseIPv4(ipStr)
792: 	if !ok {
793: 		if ip, ok = utils.ParseIPv6(ipStr); !ok {
794: 			return false
795: 		}
796: 	}
797: 
798: 	if cfg.Loopback && ip.IsLoopback() {
799: 		return true
800: 	}
801: 	if cfg.Private && ip.IsPrivate() {
802: 		return true
803: 	}
804: 	if cfg.LinkLocal && ip.IsLinkLocalUnicast() {
805: 		return true
806: 	}
807: 
808: 	var canonicalIP [net.IPv6len * 3]byte
809: 	if _, trusted := cfg.ips[utils.UnsafeString(ip.AppendTo(canonicalIP[:0]))]; trusted {
810: 		return true
811: 	}
812: 	if len(cfg.ranges) == 0 {
813: 		return false
814: 	}
815: 
816: 	if ip.Is4() {
817: 		ipv4 := ip.As4()
818: 		for _, ipNet := range cfg.ranges {
819: 			if ipNet.Contains(ipv4[:]) {
820: 				return true
821: 			}
822: 		}
823: 		return false
824: 	}
825: 
826: 	ipv6 := ip.As16()
827: 	for _, ipNet := range cfg.ranges {
828: 		if ipNet.Contains(ipv6[:]) {
829: 			return true
830: 		}
831: 	}
832: 	return false
833: }

898: // Method returns the HTTP request method for the context, optionally overridden by the provided argument.
899: // If no override is given or if the provided override is not a valid HTTP method, it returns the current method from the context.
900: // Otherwise, it updates the context's method and returns the overridden method as a string.
901: func (r *DefaultReq) Method(override ...string) string {
902: 	app := r.c.app
903: 	if len(override) == 0 {
904: 		// Nothing to override, just return current method from context
905: 		return currentMethod(r.c)
906: 	}
907: 
908: 	// Method tokens are case-sensitive (RFC 9110 Section 9.1), so try the
909: 	// override exactly as given first — this is what keeps mixed-case custom
910: 	// methods registered via Config.RequestMethods working.
911: 	method := override[0]
912: 	methodInt := app.methodInt(method)
913: 	if methodInt == -1 {
914: 		// Fall back to the conventional uppercase form as a convenience for
915: 		// the standard methods (e.g. "get" -> "GET").
916: 		method = utilsstrings.ToUpper(method)
917: 		methodInt = app.methodInt(method)
918: 	}
919: 	if methodInt == -1 {
920: 		// Provided override is not a registered HTTP method; no override,
921: 		// return current method
922: 		return currentMethod(r.c)
923: 	}
924: 	r.c.methodInt = methodInt
925: 	// Method changed; invalidate the lookahead index
926: 	r.c.firstMatchIndex = -1
927: 	return method
928: }

930: // currentMethod resolves the context's method, falling back to the raw
931: // request header value when the method is not registered in RequestMethods,
932: // so unregistered methods are reported instead of panicking.

934: // Req/Ctx interfaces.

936: 	// app.method owns the definition of "unregistered" (it bounds-checks
937: 	// methodInt and returns "" for anything out of range).

939: 		return m
940: 	}

942: 	// string from RequestMethods, so callers may retain the result beyond
943: 	// the handler; an unsafe alias into the request buffer would be
944: 	// silently corrupted on connection reuse.
945: 	return string(c.fasthttp.Request.Header.Method())

1130: // Range returns a struct containing the type and a slice of ranges.
1131: func (r *DefaultReq) Range(size int64) (Range, error) {
1132: 	var (
1133: 		rangeData Range
1134: 		ranges    string
1135: 	)
1136: 	rangeStr := utils.TrimSpace(r.Get(HeaderRange))
1137: 	maxRanges := r.c.app.config.MaxRanges
1138: 	const maxRangePrealloc = 8
1139: 	prealloc := min(maxRanges, maxRangePrealloc)
1140: 	if prealloc > 0 {
1141: 		rangeData.Ranges = make([]RangeSet, 0, prealloc)
1142: 	}
1143: 
1144: 	// parseBound parses a present (non-empty) range bound. A bound that is
1145: 	// not a valid integer makes the range-spec, and therefore the whole
1146: 	// ranges-specifier, invalid (RFC 9110 Section 14.1.1).
1147: 	parseBound := func(value string) (int64, error) {
1148: 		parsed, err := utils.ParseUint(value)
1149: 		if err != nil {
1150: 			return 0, ErrRangeMalformed
1151: 		}
1152: 		if parsed > (math.MaxUint64 >> 1) {
1153: 			return 0, ErrRangeMalformed
1154: 		}
1155: 		return int64(parsed), nil
1156: 	}
1157: 
1158: 	before, after, found := strings.Cut(rangeStr, "=")
1159: 	if !found {
1160: 		return Range{}, ErrRangeMalformed
1161: 	}
1162: 	if !utils.EqualFold(utils.TrimSpace(before), "bytes") {
1163: 		// A range unit the server does not understand is not malformed: it
1164: 		// must be ignored (RFC 9110 Section 14.2), which only the caller can
1165: 		// do, so signal it distinctly. This check runs before any syntax
1166: 		// checks on the range-set, since the other-range grammar permits
1167: 		// characters (such as "=") that byte ranges do not.
1168: 		return Range{}, ErrRangeUnsupported
1169: 	}
1170: 	rangeData.Type = "bytes"
1171: 	if strings.IndexByte(after, '=') >= 0 {
1172: 		return Range{}, ErrRangeMalformed
1173: 	}
1174: 	ranges = utils.TrimSpace(after)
1175: 
1176: 	var (
1177: 		singleRange  string
1178: 		moreRanges   = ranges
1179: 		elementCount int  // every list element, including empty ones (MaxRanges bound)
1180: 		sawRangeSpec bool // at least one non-empty range-spec was present
1181: 	)

1183: 		// Empty elements count toward MaxRanges too, so the cap bounds the
1184: 		// total parsing work per header, not just the accepted range-specs.
1185: 		elementCount++
1186: 		if elementCount > maxRanges {
1187: 			r.c.DefaultRes.Status(StatusRequestedRangeNotSatisfiable)
1188: 			r.c.DefaultRes.Set(HeaderContentRange, "bytes */"+utils.FormatInt(size)) //nolint:staticcheck // It is fine to ignore the static check
1189: 			return Range{}, ErrRangeTooLarge
1190: 		}
1191: 
1192: 		singleRange = moreRanges
1193: 		if i := strings.IndexByte(moreRanges, ','); i >= 0 {
1194: 			singleRange = moreRanges[:i]
1195: 			moreRanges = utils.TrimSpace(moreRanges[i+1:])
1196: 		} else {
1197: 			moreRanges = ""
1198: 		}
1199: 
1200: 		singleRange = utils.TrimSpace(singleRange)
1201: 
1202: 		// RFC 9110 Section 5.6.1.2: recipients must parse and ignore a
1203: 		// reasonable number of empty list elements, e.g. "bytes=,0-5" is
1204: 		// equivalent to "bytes=0-5".
1205: 		if singleRange == "" {
1206: 			continue
1207: 		}
1208: 		sawRangeSpec = true
1209: 
1210: 		var (
1211: 			startStr, endStr string
1212: 			i                int
1213: 		)
1214: 		if i = strings.IndexByte(singleRange, '-'); i == -1 {
1215: 			return Range{}, ErrRangeMalformed
1216: 		}
1217: 		startStr = utils.TrimSpace(singleRange[:i])
1218: 		endStr = utils.TrimSpace(singleRange[i+1:])
1219: 
1220: 		var (
1221: 			start, end int64
1222: 			err        error
1223: 		)
1224: 		if startStr != "" {
1225: 			if start, err = parseBound(startStr); err != nil {
1226: 				return Range{}, err
1227: 			}
1228: 		}
1229: 		if endStr != "" {
1230: 			if end, err = parseBound(endStr); err != nil {
1231: 				return Range{}, err
1232: 			}
1233: 		}
1234: 		switch {
1235: 		case startStr == "" && endStr == "":
1236: 			// "-" carries neither a first-byte-pos nor a suffix-length and is
1237: 			// not a valid range-spec (RFC 9110 Section 14.1.1).
1238: 			return Range{}, ErrRangeMalformed
1239: 		case startStr == "": // -nnn (suffix range)
1240: 			start = max(size-end, 0)
